Both are feasible in this classroom format and tightly tied to constructive thinking about this design/ethics topic.

new_question.comment: Directly targets constructive cognition by requiring students to identify a risk area and generate an original strategy tied to their own project. Strong topical fit with academic integrity and AI use; no grounding conflicts since it is future-oriented by design.

reference_answer.comment: Models high-quality constructive reasoning: specifies context (typography project), articulates how AI could compromise integrity, and details an original workflow maintaining authentic intellectual work. Aligns with the topic and the intended C-level cognitive demand.

dimension_rationales.accuracy: The ICAP interpretation is sound: students currently speaking exhibit Constructive behaviors (generating and explaining their own design ideas), with no student-student interaction, matching the classification summary. The diagnosis that the bottleneck lies in low constructive coverage (2/30, 0.067 ratio) rather than incorrect level is consistent with the provided metrics and definitions. The proposed evolution keeps the class at C, which aligns with the expected_ci_level and the lack of I behavior in the context.
dimension_rationales.alignment_grounding: The suggestion explicitly uses the correct class size (30), the actual number of speaking students (2), and accurately paraphrases their contributions from the transcript. There are no fabricated events or metrics. All future-oriented elements (rewrites, strategies, question, answer) are pedagogically plausible extensions tied to the topic of academic integrity and design work, and they serve the goal of expanding constructive engagement rather than shifting to interactive mode.
dimension_rationales.actionability: Both main strategies specify who acts (teacher calls on students; students construct explanations and artifacts), what they do (answer targeted prompts; produce annotated sketches, concept maps, or paragraphs), and approximately when (every 8–10 minutes; during a concurrent work period with rapid check-ins). They are specific to this design/academic integrity context (e.g., ethical risk of AI in projects, synthesizing design principles), not generic slogans, and are not so detailed as to be impractical. A teacher could reasonably implement or adapt them in a typical session.
